title: Hierarchical Decision Routing
business: Logistics firms managing complex package routing paths.
problem: Linear search through thousands of routing rules causes latency spikes during peak shipping hours.
solution: A binary tree organizes nodes with at most two child links, allowing the system to prune half the search space at each decision point.
steps: Define a root node representing the primary regional hub.
Assign left child links to sub-regions with lower postal codes.
Assign right child links to sub-regions with higher postal codes.
Traverse the tree by comparing the target destination against the current node value.
Terminate the search upon reaching a leaf node or finding a match.
outcome: Sub-millisecond routing decisions regardless of the total number of regional hubs.
limitation: The tree can become unbalanced if data is inserted in sorted order, leading to O(n) performance; check balance by comparing the height of left and right subtrees.

questions.question: In Hierarchical Decision Routing, how does the technology address the latency problem?
options: By pruning half the search space at each decision point
By sorting all routing rules into a single linear array
By increasing the number of child links per node
By using a brute force search for every package
questions.explanation: The binary tree structure allows for efficient navigation by discarding half of the remaining possibilities at each node.
questions.evidence: A binary tree organizes nodes with at most two child links, allowing the system to prune half the search space at each decision point.

questions.question: In Hierarchical Decision Routing, what is a primary limitation of the implementation?
options: The tree cannot handle more than four nodes
It requires a constant O(1) time regardless of structure
It can become unbalanced if data is inserted in sorted order
It is impossible to check the balance of the tree
questions.explanation: The documentation notes that sorted insertion can degrade performance by creating an unbalanced tree.
questions.evidence: The tree can become unbalanced if data is inserted in sorted order, leading to O(n) performance; check balance by comparing the height of left and right subtrees.
